title: GRADE reasons to rate certainty up
description: The three domains for which GRADE may raise the certainty of a body of evidence — applied mainly to observational studies with no reason to rate down. Moved from smart-kg/methodologies/grade.md by bean wg7r, 2026-09-24 (owner: 'needs to be part of skill/SKOS'). Read with the `grade` skill.

source.note: Guyatt GH, et al. GRADE guidelines: 9. Rating up the quality of evidence. J Clin Epidemiol 2011;64(12):1311-1316

codes.label: Large magnitude of effect
codes.definition: The effect is so large that bias alone is unlikely to explain it.

codes.label: Dose-response gradient
codes.definition: The effect increases or decreases consistently with the level of exposure, which strengthens the inference that the relationship is causal.

codes.label: Plausible confounding would reduce the effect
codes.definition: All plausible residual confounding or bias would reduce a demonstrated effect — or would suggest a spurious effect where none was observed — so the true effect is likely at least as large as estimated.
